# Ghoti

> Ghoti is a single-binary, in-memory server for coordination primitives. It gives a fleet of services up to 1,000 configurable slots (token-bucket and leaky-bucket rate limiters, timeout-memory leases, atomic counters, tickers, simple memory, broadcast and multicast channels) over a plain-text TCP protocol (`standard` or `telnet`) or HTTP with Server-Sent Events. No client library is required.

Key facts:

- All state is in memory. A restart empties every slot; nothing is persisted.
- Values are opaque byte strings of at most 36 bytes; requests are 4 to 40 bytes; one request in flight per connection.
- Commands: `r<slot>` read, `w<slot><value>` write, `s<slot>`/`d<slot>` subscribe/leave (multicast), `u`/`p` login, `q` quit. Responses start with `v` (value), `e` (error, `e<slot><code>`) or `a` (async event).
- Start the server with `ghoti run`; it reads `config.yaml` from `/etc/ghoti`, `$HOME/.ghoti` or the current directory and exits if none is found. Default address `localhost:9090`.
- No TLS on any listener. Broadcast/multicast delivery is at most once. Clustering (leader election, no replication) is experimental.
- Latest release: v0.3.0. License: Apache-2.0. Source: https://github.com/dankomiocevic/ghoti

## Start

- [Overview](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/): What Ghoti is and isn't: slot kinds, transports, durability, ordering and delivery guarantees at a glance, and when it fits your system.
- [Getting started](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/getting-started/): Run Ghoti and get your first answers in four commands, then install from a release archive, verify the download, and troubleshoot a first run.
- [Concepts](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/concepts/): Slots, volatile state, connections and ownership, and the one-request-in-flight rule.

## Protocol

- [Protocol](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/protocol/): Ghoti's plain-text protocol: framing and limits, commands, responses, ordering, and which commands are safe to retry.
- [Transports](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/protocol/transports/): The standard, telnet and http transports, line endings, HTTP status mapping, timeouts, SSE heartbeats and backpressure.

## Configure

- [Configuration](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/configuration/): Where Ghoti reads config.yaml, GHOTI_ environment variables, and the addr, protocol, max_connections and log settings.
- [Slot reference](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/configuration/slots/): Every slot kind (simple memory, timeout memory, token bucket, leaky bucket, ticker, atomic, broadcast, multicast) with its options and exact behaviour.
- [Authentication](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/authentication/): Users, per-slot permissions, the exact login rules, and why passwords travel in cleartext.

## Run

- [Operations](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/operations/): Running Ghoti in production: Prometheus metrics, connection limits, deployment, shutdown and TLS termination.
- [Cluster](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/cluster/): Experimental leader election between Ghoti nodes with the bully algorithm and no replication: configuration, routing, failure scenarios and limits.

## Reference

- [Error codes](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/reference/errors/): Every error code Ghoti returns, with its name, meaning and when it closes the connection.
- [Contributing](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/docs/contributing/): How to build, test and contribute to Ghoti, how CI checks a pull request, and how to report a security issue.

## Benchmarks

- [Benchmarks](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/benchmarks/): Ghoti v0.3.0 on a 2-vCPU, 1-GiB AWS t4g.micro: 134,000 reads/s at 0.60 ms median round trip with 100 connections, 0 errors in 255M requests.

## Tutorials

- [Implementing leader election with Ghoti](https://ghoti.miocevic.com/blog/2025/07/25/implementing-leader-election-with-ghoti/): Use a timeout memory slot as a lease so that only one of your nodes acts as leader, and learn exactly where the approach stops being safe.
